title: AI-guided prioritization of potential FAM171A2 ligands through pharmacophore-aware and receptor-based screening
content: FAM171A2 has recently emerged as a potential therapeutic target in Parkinson's disease because it selectively recognizes α-synuclein fibrils and promotes their neuronal uptake. However, ligand prioritization for this receptor remains challenging because of scarce known binders, the absence of an experimentally resolved ligand-bound structure and the requirement for blood–brain barrier permeability. Here, we established an AI-guided computational screening framework that integrates pharmacophore-aware retrieval, hierarchical receptor-based screening, blood–brain barrier permeability prediction and molecular dynamics-based assessment to prioritize potential FAM171A2 ligands. Starting from 1.41 million compounds, the workflow progressively narrowed the search space to two structurally representative candidates, E634-1386 and F707-2364. Both candidates showed more favorable in silico profiles than the reference blocker Bemcentinib across complementary computational assessments: E634-1386 achieved higher KarmaDock and CarsiDock scores, whereas F707-2364 yielded the most favorable AutoDock Vina score and MM/GBSA estimate. Molecular dynamics simulations further suggested stable predicted FAM171A2-bound complexes for both candidates, with lower complex RMSD, reduced radius of gyration and lower protein solvent-accessible surface area relative to Bemcentinib, while maintaining broadly similar residue-level flexibility patterns. Representative interaction analysis suggested that E634-1386 may rely more on polar contacts, whereas F707-2364 may engage the predicted binding region through broader hydrophobic complementarity. Together, these results prioritize E634-1386 and F707-2364 as computationally selected, experimentally testable FAM171A2 ligand candidates and provide a practical strategy for early-stage ligand prioritization against structurally challenging central nervous system targets.
